briefing.headline: Strong training week, but a quiet finish.
briefing.result: The performance gains are real; the part to protect is the end of the week, where the routine has slipped before.
briefing.meaning: Training kept moving forward, with new bests on seven lifts, but the routine slipped late in the week. The September 12 DEXA showed lean mass up 5 lb with body fat at 8.1%; the scale alone can't say how much of any recent gain is lean mass, and the next DEXA will.
briefing.action: Get the usual training rhythm back this week.
briefing.watch: Watch the weekly weight average and whether Friday and Saturday get their usual training back.
briefing.coachTake: Keep pushing the same lifts; Hack Squats went from 6 to 12 reps at 115 lb. Your weight has been rising about 1.7 lb a week over the last four weeks, in the direction the goal wants. Thursday through Saturday's food logs were too patchy to read; complete logs from here on will make the next check clearer.

confidence.explanation: Confidence holds. The September 12 DEXA still sets the outlook, and a short break in routine isn't enough to change it.
confidence.why: You are more than halfway to the 10 lb lean-mass goal. The measured progress in lean mass is real. There is enough time to finish ahead of schedule if this level of progress continues.
